trick: One CLAUDE.md vs one per package
source_note: Claude Code's docs recommend a root CLAUDE.md plus one per directory or package; subdirectory files load on demand, when the agent reads a file there. Both layouts are built by build_layouts.py from one source, lines.md, where every block is tagged @root or @packages/<folder>. The with side gets a root CLAUDE.md (repo-wide lines) plus packages/frai-cli, frai-core, frai-gate and frai-agent CLAUDE.md files; the without side gets one root CLAUDE.md with the same blocks under the same per-package headings. The script checks that the combined file equals the split files joined in order (54 identical non-blank lines on both sides). Sessions start at the repo root, so on the with side a package file loads only after the agent reads a file in that package; the hard tasks span packages (h1 frai-gate; h2 frai-core and frai-cli; h3 and h4 frai-core, frai-cli and frai-agent), so several package files can load in one run. Every line was checked against the current code in base/frai and against the four hard prompts and reference patches: the run-helper example was changed from runScanCommand/runEvalCommand (h4 and h2 code) to runGenerateFlow/runRagIndexCommand; otherwise the files name validate.ts and the scanner, eval and config modules only as layout and say nothing about field parsing, thresholds, .env parsing, option handling or import matching. Task set and model changed on 15 Sep 2026 after the pilots (see PROTOCOL): t1, t2, t3 and h2 on Haiku 4.5, both sides.
